newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares close flat in light trade. [CORRECTED 18:44 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares close flat in light trade. [CORRECTED 18:44 GMT]

text.p: Tel Aviv stocks closed almost unchanged on Tuesday in low turnover as most shares were not traded at all, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares closed unchanged at 187.52 on total share turnover of 46 million shekels against 37.5 million on Monday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index fell 0.22 percent to 197.07.
"The market looks terrible and most shares were not traded at all. We hope the market will start to recover with the publishing of (third-quarter) earnings (later this month)," a trader said.
"I hope that after the U.S. elections President Bill Clinton will get more involved in the peace talks with the Palestinians. Maybe this will move the market," he said.

Clal Industries, the most active share, fell 2.75 percent to 1,278 on volume of 4.0 million shekels after its subsidiary ECI Telecom, traded on Nasdaq, plunged 5.3 percent on Monday. (Corrects to clarify that Clal Industries was the most active share, not Clal Electronics Industries)
Scitex Corp, another Clal subsidiary, lost 4.4 percent on Monday.

"Activity is low but the markets will start rising soon because of the slowing economy (which will cause interest rates to fall). Share prices are very cheap and off-the-floor transactions are being done at much higher prices," said Amir Eayal, head of portfolio management at Epsilon Securities.

Other active shares include Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which closed unchanged at 138,999 on turnover of 2.8 million shekels and Koor Industries, which also closed unchanged at 28,040 on volume of 2.2 million shekels.
